summary: Builds: `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean` exits 0 with no messages, and the olean is current (22:43, same mtime as the source). No sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide in the file. `#print axioms` (run through stdin, nothing written) gives only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound for spread_top_corrected, not_spreadTopPrinted, cex_spread_top_halfCut, isGaloisian_of_comp, isBranchedCovering_strongPullTop, isPortly_strongPullTop_iff_local, quotient_virtually_tame, hypothesis_model_spaces_mechanism and the three remark counterexamples. So every cited library result they use (maxBranched_basic, complete_path_carac, spread_top_deck, exists_extend_path_of_isCompleteSpread, exists_path_of_isPortly_of_isOpen) is genuinely proved. SpreadTopPrinted is exactly the type of Models' GX.spread_top: `@fun … => @GX.spread_top …` typechecks against it. not_spreadTopPrinted therefore really refutes the tagged-sorry statement in Models, and the halfCut instance satisfies every hypothesis, the extra hSc included. No declaration name clashes with GX/ or other scaffold files (all 89 short names grepped). REPORT lists all five dispatched labels, every decl it names exists, and the closed/partial and marked/unmarked statuses match the module docstring. Fidelity is sound wherever a theorem claims the paper. def:topological_spaces_continuous_map is the paper's definition, with p continuous dropped. The remark's coarsest-spread content and its two examples (the cut line; Q-generated T, not locally connected at √2) are correct. The corrected lem:spread_top's (a), (b), first part of the Claim, local path-connectedness and the Galoisian sub-covering are real proofs from the paper's hypotheses plus the reported hRc and the DEC-66(a) standing hypotheses on N. I re-derived by hand both informal counterexamples in the findings and found them correct. (1) ℂ* with T cutting a ray glued to one bank: T connected, R T-portly, p⁻¹(R) splits into strips. (2) The sector topology at the branch point of M̃^{0} → ℂ: hrel holds by radial shrinking; R = ℂ* is T-portly; the component of the branch point meets R̂ in ℤ sectors, so (c) fails, and (e) fails too because a branched covering pulls a portly set back to a portly set. Two major issues block 'clean'. First, the weakening of (c) to '↔ StrongLocallyConnectedOrd' and of (e) to '(c) → (e)' rests on a counterexample that is only described, while DEC-27/CAMPAIGN ask for a proved one. Second, rem:quotient_virtually_tame's finding 'for a non-Galoisian N (Γ(N/M) may even be trivial) it is false' is unsupported and appears wrong for the paper's D (a developing map), so restricting to N = M̃ is not the strongest true form. The rest is minor: bold marks on partial rows in declaration docstrings, stale references, the definition label certified in two files, a stale hypothesis-row classification, and no toy instance for the abstract mechanism.

issues.where: spread_top_corrected (l.967-1000) clauses (c) and (e); StrongLocallyConnectedOrd (l.827); module SCOPE (b) (l.69-75); REPORT lem:spread_top findings 3
issues.problem: Even under the corrected hypotheses (hRc included), (c) is weakened to an equivalence with StrongLocallyConnectedOrd, which is (c) restated locally, and (e) is made conditional on (c). The only evidence that the paper's unconditional (c)/(e) is false under these hypotheses is the sector-topology counterexample at the branch point of M̃^{0} → ℂ, described in prose and marked 'not formalized'. I checked it by hand and believe it is correct: hS, hSc and hrel hold (loops at 0 shrink radially in ℂ*); T is first countable, locally path-connected and connected; R = ℂ∖{0} is T-portly and T agrees with the usual topology on it; p⁻¹(R) is connected; the component of the branch point in p⁻¹({0} ∪ sector∩disc) meets R̂ in ℤ disjoint sectors, so p⁻¹(R) is not p^*T-portly; and (e) ⇒ (c) through IsBranchedCovering.isPortly_preimage. DEC-27 and CAMPAIGN 'gx specifics' require 'a counterexample where it is false' to be PROVED. Without it, the claim that the corrected (c)/(e) is the strongest true form is uncertified, and (c) as stated certifies almost nothing beyond a reformulation.
issues.fix: Formalize the sector counterexample: M = N = ℂ, S = {0}, q = id, R = {0}ᶜ, T = usual ⊓ generateFrom{{0} ∪ sector}. Prove that every hypothesis of spread_top_corrected holds and that ¬ IsPortly[p^*T] (p⁻¹ R), hence ¬ IsBranchedCovering for p^*T. Alternatively restate it as `¬ ∀ …, IsPortly …` of the corrected hypotheses. The halfCut file already has the needed tooling (nhds basis, LPC, portly proofs). If that is not achievable in this round, tag it explicitly as an open obligation in REPORT under sorries/obstructions instead of only in findings.

issues.where: REPORT rem:quotient_virtually_tame findings[0] and hypotheses[0]; quotient_virtually_tame docstring (l.1102-1110, 'ADDED, finding: for a non-Galoisian N → M, M ≠ Γ(N/M)\N'); module checklist l.59
issues.problem: The finding 'M ≅ Γ(N/M)\D(N) needs N → M Galoisian … for a non-Galoisian N (Γ(N/M) may even be trivial) it is false' has no counterexample. For the paper's D, an injective DEVELOPING map, it appears wrong. Pull D back along the universal M̃ → N (prop:universality): D_N∘π is a developing map of M̃ with holonomy ρ. Injectivity of D_N gives ker ρ ⊆ Γ(M̃/N), and rigidity gives Γ(M̃/N) ⊆ ker ρ. So Γ(M̃/N) = ker ρ is normal in Γ(M̃/M). When M̃ → M is Galoisian (the file's own added hypothesis) and M̃ → N is Galoisian (sub-covering, as in isGaloisian_of_comp), Γ(M̃/M)/ker ρ descends to N and acts transitively on its fibres, so N → M is Galoisian and Γ(N/M) is not trivial unless N = M. The real missing hypothesis is therefore 'M̃ → M Galoisian' (automatic when reg M is slsc in M). The narrowing to N = M̃ is then not the strongest true form: the general N with an injective developing map reduces to it. The Lean core quotient_dev allows an arbitrary injective D that is not a developing map, and for that abstraction non-Galoisian N is indeed a problem. But the finding is addressed to the PAPER.
issues.fix: Either prove a counterexample (a virtually tame M, a non-Galoisian N → M branched over sing M, and an injective developing map on N), or withdraw the finding and replace it with 'needs M̃ → M Galoisian'. Ideally also prove the general-N form: from an injective developing map on N, derive that N → M is Galoisian and apply quotient_dev. At minimum record in SCOPE that the restriction to N = M̃ is a narrowing, not forced by a defect.

The audit's argument suggests that, given it, any N with an injective developing map is automatically Galoisian, so the remark holds for general N.
